statusRule: Proposed until reviewed and merged to main. Merging freezes this file: from then on any change is a new file (v2) with its own studyId and specificationId, never an edit of v1. Approving or merging it activates no strategy, setting, screen or trade, and starts no run.
path: Weeks to months, the proposed first research path, on UTC daily bars. Not intraday, and not a choice of daily bars for the product.

questions.A: Coverage and latency: how often is direction evaluable, how often is it Unclear, and how long after the pivots that define it does a state become knowable?
questions.B: Directional information: are Up and Down observations followed by price changes in their stated direction, beyond each pair's own unconditional base rate over the same observation dates and horizon?
questions.C: Structural reference: after the observation, how often and how soon is the reference fixed at that observation breached, by a close and, separately, by an extreme?

interpretation: Retrospective historical research on one retrieval of provider history. Not a backtest, not simulated trades, fills or positions, not a portfolio return, not prospective evidence, not an untouched holdout and not evidence of profitable or executable trading. A statistical association between a state and later price changes does not establish a trading edge.
priorKnowledge: The export below was used by popup-scanner-retrospective-crypto-usdt-v1 (docs/SCANNER_RESEARCH.md#crypto-crypto-usdt-v1). Its aggregate results about model ranks, Long setups and Risk warnings were seen by the owner and by the drafting agent, including that the equal-weight universe rose on average over that study's dates (2024-09-01 to 2026-11-10). They are not about swing structure, but the period of this study overlaps them. It is not an untouched holdout.

The drafting agent has general public knowledge of the main crypto price moves before mid-2026. Measuring each pair against its own base rate over the same dates removes each pair's average drift, the most direct way such knowledge could favour a direction rule. It removes nothing else.

No pivot, direction, reference or breach of this candidate has been computed on any real candle. The universe, window, configurations, horizons and dates follow from the candidate contract, the export coverage already recorded in docs/scanner-research-crypto.v1.json (bar counts, first and last bars, completeness), and the weeks-to-months path. For this specification only the export's sha256 was recomputed, to confirm the file is the recorded one. Its contents were not read.
The candidate rule comes from common chart-reading practice. Familiarity with crypto charts cannot be removed from the people who chose it.

TRXUSDT was the subject of the owner's trial recommendation and of the real Manual Spot experiment recorded on 2026-11-14. TRX-USDT is not a member, and that experiment begins after the export's cutoff. Nothing here reads, changes or evaluates it.

candidate.rule: Called as published. Nothing in it is reimplemented, patched, tuned or given a default. The run refuses unless the two files it executes have exactly these git blob ids.

data.source: One existing owner-initiated retrieval: the crypto-usdt-v1 export of popup-scanner-retrospective-crypto-usdt-v1. No new retrieval, provider, Binance candle or reconstructed bar. The same retrieval supplies both observations and outcomes.

export.location: The owner's machine, git-ignored. Never committed or uploaded.
export.cutoff: 2026-11-11T18:38:25.830Z, the retrieval start. Only bars that closed by then are used.

inputHashes.rule: sha256(stableSerialize(instrument entry)): ticker, symbol, receivedAt and the get_ohlcv response verbatim, as recorded in docs/scanner-research-crypto.v1.json

data.mapping: tradingViewCryptoCandles (scripts/tradingViewImport.ts) with the member's committed symbol and from = 2024-02-16T00:00:00.000Z. The response must name exactly that symbol, 1D and USDT. A bar's t is its opening time in Unix seconds, and closeTime is set to open + 86,399,999 ms, so the candidate's close-time check cannot fail on this data.

bars.documentedCoverage: Recorded before this specification: each member has 1000 bars opening 2024-02-16 through 2026-11-11, at UTC midnight, with no duplicate or missing day. The run checks this and does not assume it.

data.whyThisExport: It is the only crypto history Popup has retrieved, its identity was recorded before this specification, and one retrieval then supplies every candle. A new 1000-bar retrieval would add days at the end and lose as many at the start. Paging deeper history would leave the start, capture and finish workflow and mix retrievals.

universe.selectionRule: The first five members of crypto-usdt-v1 in its committed walk order (CRYPTO_TRADINGVIEW_SYMBOLS, frozen in f076326 on 2026-11-11 before any candle was retrieved): TradingView's market-capitalization ranking that day. Five keeps the study small and limited to the largest, most liquid pairs, each with the full documented history.
universe.trx: TRX-USDT is sixth in that order and is not a member. The rule was written knowing the order. The size was chosen for the reasons above, not to include or exclude any pair. The study gives no evidence about TRXUSDT or the owner's experiment in it.
universe.fixed: No member is added, removed or replaced. A member that cannot be read stops the study (missingData.study). The universe never shrinks to the members that can be read.
universe.survivorship: Chosen by market capitalization on 2026-11-11, after the period. Pairs that are large today partly because their prices rose are present, and pairs that fell away are absent. Each pair's base rate absorbs its own average drift; nothing removes the selection itself.

timeframe.label: 1D
timeframe.session: UTC day: opens 00:00:00.000, closes 23:59:59.999. Crypto trades every day, so the candidate's fixed interval holds. UTC has no daylight saving, and epoch milliseconds have no leap seconds.

window.rule: Each observation passes the candidate exactly the member's mapped candles opening on the 180 UTC days D-179 through D, in export order, and nothing else. A candle opening after D is never passed in; the candidate would also exclude it by its own cutoff rule.
window.rationale: A fixed window gives every observation the same history, so INSUFFICIENT means no two confirmed pivots of each kind in the last 180 days, not a short start of the file. 180 days, about six months, leaves room for two confirmed highs and lows at the slowest configuration (a pivot spans 21 bars at L = R = 10), and matches the far end of the weeks-to-months path. Chosen before any pivot was computed.

observations.cutoff: tau_D = D 00:00:00.000 UTC + 86,399,999 ms, the close of D's candle. The candidate uses a candle only if its open + 86,399,999 ms <= tau_D, so D's candle is the latest one used.
observations.unit: One member, one UTC date D, one configuration: the candidate's full output at tau_D.

daily.rule: first = first bar + 179 days, so every window is complete; last = last closed bar - 61 days, so every 60-day endpoint bar has closed.

phaseGrids.rule: G_p = every date 2024-08-13 + p + 20k days up to 2026-09-10, for p = 0..19. G_0 is the primary grid. Phases 0 to 18 have 38 dates, phase 19 has 37.
phaseGrids.use: Phase sensitivity of question B only.

observations.requiredHistory: Warm-up: the 179 daily bars before D. Follow-up: the 61 bars D+1 through D+61. Together they need every bar from 2024-02-16 through 2026-11-10, exactly the export's closed bars.

configurationRationale: At L5R5 a pivot is the extreme of an 11-day span, about a week and a half, so two highs and two lows usually span several weeks: the weeks-to-months scale. Confirmation lags 5 days, a quarter of the primary horizon. L3R3 and L10R10 bracket it at about half and double the span. L5R2 keeps the left window and shortens the right one, to show what a shorter confirmation lag changes. None was run on market data, and none becomes a product setting.

horizons.rationale: 20 UTC days, about three weeks, is the near end of weeks to months and the horizon of Popup's earlier crypto studies. 60 covers months and 5 the short end; both are exploratory.

primary.question: B
primary.comparison: The signed excess of Up and Down observations over each pair's unconditional base rate, each grid date weighted once.

times.pivotCandleTime: pivot.candleOpenTime: the open of the pivot's own candle. That candle closes at candleOpenTime + 86,399,999 ms.
times.pivotAvailableAt: pivot.availableAt: the close of the candle R bars later, R days after the pivot candle's close. Before then the pivot does not exist.
times.establishedAt: The latest availableAt of the four supporting pivots: when the current state became knowable.
times.breachKnowableAt: The close of the candle that breached: the earliest moment that breach is known.

invariants: every supporting pivot's availableAt <= establishedAt <= tau_D
a breach reported at tau_D has reference.availableAt < knowableAt <= tau_D
a forward breach candle opens at or after tau_D + 1 ms, D+1 00:00 UTC
the outcome reference bar opens at tau_D + 1 ms
timing.invariantRule: The run checks every invariant on every observation and refuses on any violation. A violation is a defect, never an exclusion.
timing.lookAheadCheck: For every primary-grid observation, the run also evaluates the candidate with every mapped candle opening after D appended to the window. The two outputs must be identical, or the run refuses.
timing.frozenReference: The reference is the candidate's reference at tau_D: kind, price, candleOpenTime and availableAt. Behaviour after the observation is measured against that price only. A later observation has its own reference. No reference is replaced by a later pivot, re-dated or carried to another observation.
timing.noEntry: An observation is not an entry. No entry, exit, fill or position is simulated, so nothing in this study is post-entry.

preObservationBreach.source: The candidate's breach at tau_D: firstClose and firstExtreme, found on window candles opening after reference.availableAt.

categories.NONE: No breach of that kind by tau_D.
categories.BEFORE_ESTABLISHMENT: knowableAt <= establishedAt: the reference was already breached when the current state became knowable.
categories.AFTER_ESTABLISHMENT: establishedAt < knowableAt <= tau_D: breached after the state was knowable, before the observation.

preObservationBreach.rule: Classified separately for the close and the extreme. Both breached categories are pre-observation facts. They are never a forward breach or a post-observation outcome, never reset and never dropped: C reports them as their own groups. Their observations stay in B, where a breach changes no direction, and B is also broken down by the close category.

outcomes.notation: O_i(d), H_i(d), L_i(d), C_i(d): open, high, low and close of member i's bar opening on UTC day d. s = +1 for Up, -1 for Down. ln is the natural logarithm.
outcomes.referencePrice: O_i(D+1), the open of the first bar opening after tau_D, 1 ms later. D's close, which the observation used, is never the reference. A reference price, not a fill.
outcomes.change: r_i(D,h) = ln O_i(D+1+h) - ln O_i(D+1). Price only, quoted in USDT.
outcomes.signedOutcome: s x r_i(D,h), positive when price moved the stated way. For Down it is a directional observation, not Short profit: there is no borrow, funding, fee, slippage or execution, and Spot has no short side.
outcomes.available: Both bars exist exactly once in the export, pass validatePrices, and closed by the export cutoff.
outcomes.ties: r = 0 counts as neither a rise nor a fall in any rate, and stays in every denominator. In a breach, equal is not beyond. Every comparison with zero in the classification is strict.

baseline.baseRate: b_i(h) = the mean of r_i(D,h) over A_i(h): the dates of the grid being analysed on which member i has an AVAILABLE outcome, whatever the candidate's status that day. It is the pair's unconditional mean h-day change over the same dates. One value per member, grid and horizon, shared by every configuration.
baseline.rateBaseRates: pi+_i(h) and pi-_i(h): the shares of A_i(h) with r > 0 and with r < 0.
baseline.signedExcess: e_i(D) = s x (r_i(D,h) - b_i(h)) for each Up or Down observation with an AVAILABLE outcome. Without information its expected value is zero whatever the pair's drift and the balance of Up and Down. A raw s x r would instead reward following a drift.
baseline.dateValue: E(D) = the mean of e_i(D) over K_D, the members that are Up or Down at D with an AVAILABLE outcome, each weighted equally. Undefined when K_D is empty.
baseline.M: M = the mean of E(D) over G*, the grid dates on which E(D) is defined; n = |G*|. Each date counts once, however many members it has.
baseline.components: U = the mean, over grid dates with at least one Up observation with an AVAILABLE outcome, of that date's mean of (r - b_i) over those Up members. Dn = the same over Down members with (b_i - r). Each is positive when its state points the right way.
baseline.hitExcess: a_i(D) = 1[s x r > 0] minus pi+_i for Up or pi-_i for Down. Averaged per date over K_D, then over G*.
baseline.leaveOneMemberOut: M(-j) = M recomputed with member j removed from every K_D, for each of the five members. Dates left empty drop out. The other members' base rates are unchanged.
baseline.phaseSensitivity: M_p = M computed on G_p with base rates recomputed on G_p, for p = 0..19.
baseline.denominators: Every statistic reports its count of dates and of observations. INVALID_INPUT, WINDOW_INCOMPLETE, INSUFFICIENT and Unclear observations enter only the base rates (through their outcomes) and coverage, never K_D.

uncertainty.interval: M +/- 2.064 x f x s_E / sqrt(n). s_E is the sample standard deviation of E(D) over G* (n - 1 denominator). 2.064 is the 97.5% Student-t quantile at 24 degrees of freedom, the fewest the minimum allows, and is conservative for larger n.
uncertainty.serialCorrelation: rho = the sum of (E(D_k) - M)(E(D_k+1) - M) over consecutive grid dates both in G*, divided by the sum of (E(D) - M)^2 over G*. f = sqrt((1 + rho) / (1 - rho)) when 0 < rho < 1, and f = 1 when rho <= 0. No interval when rho >= 1.
uncertainty.fewDates: A statistic over fewer than 25 dates gets no interval and is labelled too few to read.
uncertainty.noPValue: No p-value. The interval is the range of values compatible with the data under these approximations, not the probability that the candidate works.

dependence.overlap: On the primary grid the spacing equals the primary horizon, so one member's 20-day and 5-day outcome windows never share a day: each ends at the next grid date's reference open. 60-day windows share days across three consecutive grid dates, so their intervals understate uncertainty and are labelled so. The daily dates of A overlap completely and carry no interval.
dependence.acrossPairs: Crypto pairs move together. E(D) averages within the date, so members are never counted as independent trials.
dependence.persistence: A state and its reference often persist across grid dates. C reports the number of distinct references (member, kind, candleOpenTime) beside the count of observations. A persistent state is not evidence of usefulness.

weighting.members: Equal within each date in E(D). A per-member breakdown weights that member's dates equally.
weighting.dates: Each date in G* counts once in M, U, Dn and the hit excess.
weighting.configurations: Never pooled or averaged. Each configuration is its own analysis, with the same base rates.
weighting.coverage: A counts each member-date once per configuration, pooled and per member.
weighting.reference: C counts each Up or Down observation once, pooled and per member, and reports distinct references.

A.dates: The 759 daily dates for every member and configuration (3,795 member-dates each), and the primary grid.
A.statuses: Shares of INVALID_INPUT, WINDOW_INCOMPLETE, INSUFFICIENT, Unclear (EQUAL_PIVOT_LEVEL), Unclear (MIXED_STRUCTURE), Up and Down, over all member-dates.
A.definitions: Evaluable: status EVALUATED, that is Up, Down, or Unclear by EQUAL_PIVOT_LEVEL or MIXED_STRUCTURE. Directional: Up or Down. Unclear: INSUFFICIENT plus EVALUATED Unclear. Each share is reported over all member-dates and over member-dates with valid input.
latency: Confirmation lag: availableAt minus the pivot candle's close, R days for every pivot. Checked, not estimated.
Establishment delay: establishedAt minus the close of the reference pivot's candle, in days and at least R: how long after the higher low (Up) or lower high (Down) the state became knowable.
State age: tau_D minus establishedAt, in days.
Reference age: tau_D minus the close of the reference pivot's candle, in days.
A.latencySummary: For Up and Down separately: count, minimum, quartiles, median and maximum, in whole days. All these times are candle closes on the UTC day grid.
A.transitions: On daily dates: direction changes per member per 365 days, and the quartiles of consecutive-day Up and Down run lengths. Descriptive only.
A.classification: None. A is reported in full and not classified.

B.primaryCell: L5R5, h = 20, G0: M with its interval, U, Dn, the hit excess, M(-j) for each member, all twenty M_p and their median, and the classification.
B.exploratoryCells: The other 11 configuration and horizon cells on G0: M, its interval, U, Dn and the hit excess, labelled exploratory and not classified.
B.breakdowns: Per member; by calendar half-year of D (2024H2 to 2026H2), with the count of grid dates in each; and by the pre-observation close category. Descriptive and not classified.

C.observations: Up and Down observations on G0, for every configuration.
C.atObservation: The pre-observation close and extreme categories; whether C_i(D) is beyond the reference; and the signed distance ln(C_i(D) / price) for Up or ln(price / C_i(D)) for Down, negative when beyond.
C.forward: For h = 5, 20 and 60, over bars opening D+1 through D+h: firstForwardClose, the first bar whose close is beyond the frozen price (below it for Up, above it for Down), and firstForwardExtreme, the first bar whose low (Up) or high (Down) is beyond it. The predicate is the candidate's: strict, so equal is not beyond. Reported as breached by h, and days to the first breach (1 to h).
C.complete: The forward scan needs every bar D+1 through D+h present once and valid. Otherwise that horizon is INCOMPLETE for that observation: counted, and never read as no breach.
C.groups: Forward results are reported separately for each pre-observation category of the same kind, close with close and extreme with extreme, never pooled across categories.
C.summary: Count, share breached by h and quartiles of days to the first breach, per member and pooled, with the number of distinct references.
C.headlineCell: L5R5 at h = 20. Every other cell is exploratory.
C.baseline: None. C describes the reference. It does not test an invalidation rule or a stop and cannot show that either is useful.

missingData.substitution: None: no forward-fill, interpolation, repair, sorting, deduplication, nearby bar, other retrieval, other provider or Binance candle.
missingData.study: DATA_UNAVAILABLE stops the study: the export is absent or its sha256 differs; a member's entry is absent or its input hash differs; or the mapping refuses an entry (wrong symbol, interval or currency, a non-numeric bar or a malformed time). The study is never run on fewer members, a shorter period or another retrieval. That would be a new specification.

observation.INVALID_INPUT: The candidate's own status: a defect among the window's candles, such as a duplicate, an out-of-order or missing day, or a price issue. Every observation whose window contains the defect has it, up to 180 consecutive daily dates per defect.
observation.WINDOW_INCOMPLETE: Assigned by the run when the candidate returns no INVALID_INPUT but closedCandles is not 180 or latestCloseTime is not tau_D: the window's first or last day is absent. The observation has no direction.

outcome.MISSING: No bar opens on the reference or endpoint day.
outcome.INVALID: That bar fails validatePrices or appears more than once.
outcome.PENDING: Cannot occur: every endpoint bar closes by 2026-11-10. If it does, the run refuses.

missingData.reporting: Every status is counted per member, configuration, date set and horizon. The local results list each INVALID_INPUT, WINDOW_INCOMPLETE, MISSING, INVALID and INCOMPLETE case with its member, date and issue codes.

interpretability.rule: The primary cell is classified only if every condition holds. Otherwise it is NOT_INTERPRETABLE and the failing conditions are named. Every figure is reported either way.
interpretability.scope: Counts are on G0 under L5R5 at h = 20. The two maxima are per member, out of its 38 grid dates.
interpretability.rationale: 25 dates is the smallest sample the interval's quantile allows. 30 observations on 10 dates per state is the repository's existing too-few-to-read floor, applied to Up and Down because B asks about both. More than 3 missing grid dates for one member would let missing data, not the candidate, shape that member's share. The documented export has none, so exceeding it points to a data problem worth stopping for.

classification.INFORMATIVE: Interpretable, and all of: the interval's lower bound > 0; U > 0 and Dn > 0; M(-j) > 0 for each of the five members; the hit excess > 0; and the median of M_0 to M_19 > 0.
classification.ADVERSE: Interpretable, and the interval's upper bound < 0: Up and Down pointed against the later move, relative to the base rate.
classification.INCONCLUSIVE: Interpretable, and neither INFORMATIVE nor ADVERSE.
classification.NOT_INTERPRETABLE: At least one interpretability condition fails.

meaning.INFORMATIVE: On this history only, L5R5 Up and Down states were followed by 20-day changes in their stated direction beyond each pair's base rate, by more than the interval attributes to chance under its approximations, and not because of one pair or one grid phase. This is retrospective association on history that was partly examined before. It is not a trading return or proof of profitability. It would justify only a separately frozen prospective check, never activation.
meaning.INCONCLUSIVE: The data neither support nor rule out an effect within the interval's range. It is not evidence of no effect.
meaning.ADVERSE: The states pointed against the subsequent move on this history; the candidate as configured would have misled.
meaning.NOT_INTERPRETABLE: Too little directional evidence, or too much missing data, to read B.

classification.prominence: Each classification is reported with the same prominence. A and C are reported in full whatever B shows.
classification.noPostHocThresholds: Every threshold and condition above is fixed here. None is chosen, moved or added after any result is seen.

multipleComparisons: Only the primary cell (L5R5, 20 days, G0) is classified. The other 11 configuration and horizon cells, U and Dn, the phase grids and every breakdown are exploratory: reported with unadjusted intervals, labelled, and never classified. Among 12 cells, the chance that at least one interval excludes zero by chance alone would be about one in two if they were independent. No configuration, horizon, member subset, period or threshold is chosen from these results. A later study of anything singled out here must say it was selected after these results, and test it on data that begins after them.

reproducibility.inputManifest: The run records the export's file name, size, sha256 and retrieval times and each member's input hash, verifies them against data.export and data.inputHashes, and refuses on any difference.
reproducibility.code: The run records the repository commit and the git blob ids of the candidate, its validation dependency, the analysis module and this file. It refuses unless the first two equal candidate.sourceBlobs and this file's computed specificationId equals the one it declares.
reproducibility.specificationId: sha256(stableSerialize(this object without specificationId)), the identity rule of docs/opportunity-radar.v1.json.
reproducibility.attribution: Every observation row carries studyId, specificationId, candidate id and version, configuration id, leftBars, rightBars, timeframe, member, symbol, D and tau_D, then the candidate's output verbatim, then the outcome and breach fields.
reproducibility.output: .zerochart-reports/swing-structure-evaluation-<first 12 hex of specificationId>.json, git-ignored, written once with exclusive create through saveResearchResults. A byte-identical rerun reports UNCHANGED; any difference reports CONFLICT and overwrites nothing. resultsSha256 is the sha256 of the file's bytes. The JSON holds no wall-clock time; an optional HTML report beside it may.
reproducibility.determinism: Members in ticker code-unit order, configurations in the order above, horizons ascending, dates ascending. Every sum runs in that order, in IEEE-754 doubles, and numbers are serialized by JSON.stringify. The same inputs and code reproduce the same bytes.
reproducibility.publication: The repository is public. A pull request or document quotes aggregate figures only; per-date rows stay in the local results.

reporting: Manifest: specificationId, repository commit, blob ids, export identity, per-member input hashes, and the verification result of each.
Completeness: per member, bars found against bars required (2024-02-16 to 2026-11-10), with every missing, duplicate or invalid bar listed.
A, per configuration: status shares on daily dates and on G0, pooled and per member; latency summaries; transitions and run lengths.

B primary: n, observation counts by state, M and its interval, s_E, rho and f, U, Dn, the hit excess, M(-j) for each member, all twenty M_p and their median, each interpretability condition with its value, and the classification with the value of every condition.
B exploratory: the same statistics for the other 11 cells, labelled exploratory; breakdowns per member, per half-year and per pre-observation close category.

C, per configuration and horizon: pre-observation categories, position and distance at observation, forward close and extreme breach shares and days to first breach by category, INCOMPLETE counts, and distinct references.
Exclusions: every status and outcome category, counted per member, configuration, date set and horizon.
limitations: Retrospective: one provider's history as retrieved on 2026-11-11, not as it stood on each date. Later revisions of past bars are unknown.
Small: 38 non-overlapping primary dates in about two years, on five pairs that move together. Wide intervals are expected, and INCONCLUSIVE is a likely, legitimate result.
One regime sample: the period's market phases may not recur. The half-year breakdown shows concentration; it does not remove it.
Selection: the members are today's largest pairs (universe.survivorship).

Scope: weeks to months on UTC daily bars of five Binance Spot USDT pairs, candidate 0.1.0, the four configurations above. It says nothing about intraday bars, equities or ETFs, weekly or monthly bars, other session boundaries, other venues or other candidate versions. The candidate's fixed-interval rule reads equity weekends and holidays as MISSING_INTERVAL and cannot represent calendar months; this study uses 24/7 UTC days, where the fixed interval holds.
No costs, fills, slippage, funding, sizing or exits: no strategy is tested.
Prior exposure (priorKnowledge): this is not an untouched holdout.
analysisCode: Written later in its own change, tested on synthetic fixtures (including look-ahead, frozen-reference and pre-observation-breach cases), and committed before it reads the export. It implements this text and cannot change it; where they differ, this specification governs. It runs only after this specification is merged, and only when the owner decides.
notDone: any run, data retrieval, real observation or result
any change to the candidate, its version, the active model, thresholds, Pine, UI, worker or portfolio decisions
production, Binance account or TradingView alert access; migrations, database writes, deployment or new dependencies
simulated trades, portfolio returns, win rates, Sharpe or other risk-adjusted ratios, drawdown, leverage or execution
any change to an existing study, scan, experiment or campaign
a replay runner, reporting system or parameter search
